title: How China Is Regulating AI
gist: Teaser (Gavekal Dragonomics, Tilly Zhang): ahead of a US-China AI government dialogue at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China's AI regulation diverges sharply from the US — Beijing is accelerating rule-setting focused on large-scale industrial adoption for productivity, not frontier-model risk or data-center backlash, since its models are not at the frontier and infrastructure buildout is uncontroversial.

themes.theme: US-China AI dialogue at APEC Shenzhen

insights.claim: China and the US have agreed to hold a government dialogue on risks and best practices for artificial intelligence models, with these issues on the agenda at the APEC summit in Shenzhen in November 2026.
insights.speaker: Tilly Zhang
insights.so_what: Watch APEC Shenzhen for any bilateral AI framework; a thaw on AI governance could ease tech-tension risk premia.
insights.quote: China and the US have agreed to have a government dialogue on risks and best practices relating to artificial intelligence models
insights.locator: China and the US have agreed

insights.claim: Despite a planned US-China AI dialogue, the two countries' approaches to regulating AI differ substantially, and the gap has become more visible as China accelerated its AI rule-setting activity in 2026.
insights.speaker: Tilly Zhang
insights.so_what: Expect limited regulatory convergence; firms operating in both markets face divergent compliance regimes.
insights.quote: there are big differences in how the two countries approach the regulation of AI, which have become increasingly visible as China has accelerated its rule-setting activity this year
insights.locator: China and the US have agreed

insights.claim: US AI policy debate centers on managing risks from rapidly advancing frontier-model capabilities and on the local impact of building data centers and related infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Tilly Zhang
insights.so_what: Local opposition to data-center buildout is a US-specific friction for AI capex and power/infrastructure plays.
insights.locator: In the US, the AI policy debate

insights.claim: Frontier-model risk and data-center infrastructure impact barely feature in Chinese AI policy discussions, because Chinese domestic models are not at the frontier and infrastructure development is uncontroversial in China.
insights.speaker: Tilly Zhang
insights.so_what: China's AI infrastructure buildout faces less political friction than in the US, favoring faster capex execution there.
insights.quote: domestic models are not at the frontier, and infrastructure development is uncontroversial
insights.locator: Neither issue features prominently in Chinese

insights.claim: China's AI strategy emphasizes large-scale adoption of AI models and tools across industries to boost productivity, rather than frontier-capability leadership or risk management.
insights.speaker: Tilly Zhang
insights.so_what: Favors China AI exposure via adopters and application/tools vendors across industry rather than frontier-model developers.
insights.quote: China’s strategy for AI instead emphasizes the large-scale adoption of models and tools across industries to boost productivity.
insights.locator: Neither issue features prominently in Chinese
